simple.meaning: נְעֹרֶת (nᵉʻôreth) is a Hebrew word meaning “something shaken out, i.e. tow (as the refuse of flax).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: נְעֹרֶת (H5296) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Judges 16:9, with occurrences in Judges, Isaiah.

simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in נְעֹרֶת (H5296) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: נְעֹרֶת (nᵉʻôreth) / H5296 is traced through Judges 16:9, Isaiah 1:31 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: something shaken out, i.e. tow (as the refuse of flax)
definitions.full: H5296. neoreth נְעֹ֫רֶת noun feminine tow (as shaken off from the flax when beaten; on form compare Ba NB 64 ); — in simile ׳מְּתִילהַֿנּ Judg 16:9 a thread of tow (snapping from heat); ׳נ Isa 1:31 (figurative; as inflammable). III. נער (√ of following; meaning unknown).
